items.article_context_en: Bitcoin climbed back above $83,000 after an early dip, decoupling from a sharp slide in Korean chip stocks and weakness in Nasdaq futures ahead of Thursday’s US CPI report. Bitcoin BTC$82 292,69 climbed back above $83,000 on Tuesday, shaking off an early drop as a sharp selloff in Asian chip stocks and U.S. tech futures weighed on risk appetite. The largest cryptocurrency by market value fell to just under $81,000 at 00:50 UTC before recovering above $83,000, according to CoinDesk data. Ether ETH$2 515,56 bounced from five-day lows, while XRP (XRP) turned higher after touching three-week lows. Zcash (ZEC), solana (SOL) and several other major tokens followed a similar pattern. The early crypto weakness came as South Korea’s KOSPI plunged more than 6% intraday, falling below 6,000 and hitting its lowest level since late July. The index remained down roughly 6% in morning trade. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each fell roughly 8%, extending their losing streaks to five sessions. Investors were rattled by concerns over AI-related valuations and rising competition from Chinese memory-chip producers. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng slipped 0.4%, while Nasdaq futures fell 0.6%, extending Monday’s 0.78% decline in the tech-heavy index. WTI crude traded near $92.67, holding most of Monday’s sharp recovery from below $90. Fresh attacks in Saudi Arabia and continued threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have kept energy-market uncertainty elevated. Brent crude hovered around $106 a barrel after a three-day rally, as traders weighed potential supply disruptions against expectations of additional Russian diesel exports.

items.article_context_en: The Bitmine (BMNR) chairman said he expects younger investors to drive demand for digital assets as his Ethereum treasury company inches closer to owning 5% of ether (ETH). Tom Lee, chairman of ether ETH$2,515.53 treasury firm Bitmine BMNR$23.84·Market Closed, said he sees a wave of inherited wealth flowing to younger investors as a potential driver of the next crypto bull market. Lee, a Wall Street veteran who also co-founded financial research and asset management firm Fundstrat in 2014 and serves as its chief investment officer, pointed to estimates from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and Fundstrat suggesting between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion in wealth could change hands from 2026 through 2028. "The wealth transfer underway is expected to support the upcoming crypto bull market as those inheriting wealth are younger and likely have a higher risk appetite for crypto and equities," Lee said in a Monday statement. His remarks echoed what Vlad Tenev, CEO of digital brokerage Robinhood, highlighted in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer last month, saying more than $100 trillion in wealth is set to pass from older to younger generations over the coming decades. The idea is that younger investors may put more of their inherited money into crypto than previous generations, adding another source of demand. How much of that wealth will actually reach digital assets, though, is unclear. Lee also noted Wall Street's growing use of blockchain technology to represent financial assets, the rise of AI applications and crypto treasury companies holding tokens for the long term as possible drivers of a new rally. Lee's remarks came alongside Bitmine's latest crypto holdings update, which showed the ether treasury firm inching closer to its goal of owning 5% of the token's supply. Bitmine Immersion Technologies BMNR$23.84·Market Closed picked up another 12,532 ETH last week, worth roughly $32 million at Monday's price. The purchase lifted its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, worth roughly $15.3 billion. That's about 4.9% of ether’s 122.1 million token supply, leaving the company some 76,000 ETH short of its goal of owning 5%. At last week's pace, Bitmine could hit that target in about six weeks.

items.article_context_en: Onchain data shows over $81 million of the stolen funds remain traceable despite hackers routing assets through mixing services. As much as $93.2 million in crypto was siphoned from wallets linked to the Ledger devices sold by the reseller CryptoBilis, according to several blockchain analytical and intelligence firms. Tether has frozen $10 million in USDT tied to the theft, while Ledger said Sunday that the investigations into the theft, first reported three days ago, are still underway. Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in at least one affected device. The company did not say whether the stolen wallet was compromised in the same way or how the devices were tampered with. Blockchain analysis and intelligence company Bitquery said it traced $93.2 million linked to the Ledger exploit. It said the hackers stole mostly USDT and TRON tokens from 315 wallets across six blockchains. Security research platform YFarmX reported a higher number, saying the attackers siphoned off $94.5 million from 521 addresses across seven blockchains. Both estimates are based on public blockchain data, not a confirmed Ledger loss total. Ledger did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for confirmation of the amount stolen and whether it is considering a reimbursement plan for those affected by the exploit. The Tether freeze, confirmed by Bitquery, is important because stablecoin issuers can block tokens linked to crime, unlike bitcoin or ether. Bitquery also said roughly $81 million could still be traced onchain as of Oct. 11, while some funds had moved through Tornado Cash and Zcash. Tether did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment on the freeze.

items.article_context_en: Loans use third-party custodians for bitcoin holdings and rely on court-ordered sales if borrowers default. Jeonbuk Bank has started offering bitcoin-backed loans to corporate clients, becoming the country's first bank to let firms borrow cash against their crypto holdings. The South Korean bank, a unit of JB Financial Group, will issue loans in the country’s fiat currency, the Korean won, with proceeds limited to business operating costs, according to local news outlet Edaily. A Jeonbuk Bank official confirmed to local outlet Jaekyung Ilbo that a loan has already been executed, but declined to name the borrower. Only bitcoin BTC$82,292.69 can be used as collateral for these loans for the time being. Jeonbuk Bank will not hold the BTC itself and instead, a registered crypto service provider will keep the assets in custody while the bank issues the loan. If a borrower fails to repay, the bank would move to recover its money through a court-ordered sale of the bitcoin. The process draws on revised Civil Enforcement Rules that took effect Oct. These changes set out legal steps for seizing and selling rights tied to digital assets. The bank ran its own stress tests to assess how bitcoin would hold up during sharp price drops and chose BTC based on its deep liquidity, allowing the funds to be liquidated when needed. The service brings a South Korean bank’s offering in line with a wider trend bitcoin-backed lending evolving into a more mainstream source of credit. The report did not disclose loan rates, borrowing limits or collateral requirements, though Jaekyung Ilbo reported that the bank reviewed loan-to-value ratios and margin-call thresholds for major tokens, including bitcoin and ether, while designing the product. Jeonbuk Bank could expand the service based on market demand and changes to crypto regulations. The new offering comes after the bank’s CEO Park Chun-won said earlier this year the lender would roll out the country's first crypto-backed loan.

items.article_context_en: SWI Group acquired majority control of Genesis Digital after the FTX bankruptcy estate dropped a $1.15B clawback suit against the miner. The Euronext Amsterdam-listed company, an investment firm concentrating on digital infrastructure, said the capital increase values it at 6.1 billion euros. It announced the purchase of about 40% of Genesis Digital in June for $500 million, completing the acquisition in August with 70% of the voting rights and renaming the unit SWI Digital. The company's strategy illustrates what has become a familiar trade for bitcoin-mining enterprises. Their most valuable asset is no longer their mining machines, but the power connections and the data-center sites that can be repurposed for AI customers. Bitcoin miners have signed more than $70 billion in AI and high-performance computing contracts, as they seek steadier revenue than bitcoin mining currently provides. The pivot from cryptocurrency mining to processing AI computations puts it in the same race as listed miners such as TeraWulf WULF$13.36·Market Closed and Core Scientific CORZ$15.02·Market Closed, which are converting power access and data-center capacity into AI hosting businesses. SWI CEO Max-Hervé George told the Wall Street Journal he had “zero interest” in bitcoin mining. The company is selling Genesis Digital Assets’ sites in Kazakhstan and aims to use its U.S. and Swedish facilities for AI workloads instead. Alameda Research, the crypto trading firm owned by former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried, invested more than $1 billion in Genesis Digital Assets from 2021 and owned about 20% of the miner, the WSJ said. FTX filed for bankruptcy in November 2022, leaving that investment among the many assets scrutinized by the estate. items.article_context_en: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in a device linked to crypto losses at CryptoBilis, a Southeast Asian reseller. The company says confirmed cases are limited and its internal systems remain unaffected. Crypto wallet manufacturer Ledger has confirmed that a device linked to recent user fund losses contained an unauthorized hardware implant. According to the company, all confirmed cases identified so far involve products distributed through the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis. 10, Ledger Support stated, “Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant.” The company added that it is actively contacting affected users as part of an ongoing investigation, and that CryptoBilis has suspended sales of all hardware wallet inventory until the investigation concludes. 11, Ledger noted that the volume of impacted devices appears limited. “To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis,” the company stated, adding that its internal systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. The confirmation of a physical implant marks the first concrete evidence supporting earlier speculation of supply-chain tampering. The incident first came to light on Friday, when Ledger acknowledged investigating reports of missing funds from customers who purchased devices through CryptoBilis, which operates in Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines. While Ledger has not confirmed an official loss, third-party on-chain researchers have estimated the loss at between $86 million and $93 million from more than 300 wallets across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tron. The company reiterated that it there is no indicattion that its own internal security infrastructure, systems, or services were compromised. Ledger stated it is cooperating with relevant authorities on Sunday. The company also reminded its network of distributors to source products exclusively through authorized channels and strictly prohibited the restocking of returned products. Secure .gov websites use HTTPSA lock (LockLocked padlock icon) or https:// means you've safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. The Federal Reserve, the central bank of the United States, provides the nation with a safe, flexible, and stable monetary and financial system. The data provide a representative picture of what Americans own, how and how much they borrow, and how they bank. The current version of the survey has been undertaken every three years since 1989 and provides the public with an extensive time series of thorough information on the economic conditions of American families. Alongside the survey data, the Board issued its summary report entitled Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2022 to 2025 (PDF), which examines changes in income, net worth, assets, debt, and financial vulnerability. In addition to the summary report, an interactive chartbook displaying changes in these financial characteristics over time is available here. Additional data from the survey, including extensive data examining other economic conditions of American families, is made available to researchers and the public here. The survey is conducted for the Board by NORC, a social science research organization at the University of Chicago. Participants in the study are chosen at random from 119 geographic areas, including metropolitan areas and rural counties across the United States, using scientific sampling procedures that aim to produce a sample representative of American families.
